details: Verse words and diacritics are unchanged and visible in the original.

details: Visible قُلْ and إِصْلَاحٌۭ are corroborated by glyph 990 (lam), 955 (sad), 1020 (lam-alif), 929 (hah), and 754 (dammatan).
One small low-meem sign U+06ED is visibly present below each ending of إِصْلَاحٌۭ and خَيْرٌۭ; glyph 1627 maps to U+06ED, not the erroneous duplicated fathatan-plus-meem sequence.
The shadda/fatha in لَّهُمْ and the Quranic stop mark ۖ remain.
The printed Arabic reference is البقرة: ٢٢٠, verified visually and by digit glyph 761 mapping to zero, not six.

details: Visible قُلْ هُوَ restores lam and heh rather than repeated marks; source glyph 1003 has an Arabic initial-heh compatibility mapping.
أَذًۭى retains visible fathatan and one small low-meem sign, with no inserted word break.
فَٱعْتَزِلُوا۟ is one connected word in the source; ٱلنِّسَآءَ visibly carries shadda on nun.
The Arabic comma after ٱلْمَحِيضِ is retained.
وَلَا restores the lam-alif ligature; تَقْرَبُوهُنَّ restores the visible heh and continuous word, preserving final shadda/fatha.
The next line حَتَّىٰ يَطْهُرْنَ and printed البقرة: ٢٢٢ match the source.

encodingQualifications: The damaged PDF ToUnicode table cannot establish original logical Unicode bytes. This review supports editable logical Arabic text matching the visible glyphs, not byte-identical source Unicode.

The font shares some glyphs between Unicode aliases, including Arabic/extended-Arabic digits and heh presentation forms. The proposed Arabic codepoints are supported by the embedded cmap and visible glyphs.
Lam-alif ligatures are represented as logical letters with the visibly supported marks; combining-mark order and ordinary spaces do not claim the PDF positioning byte sequence.
No Quran wording was substituted from memory or an external edition.
